children.value: The Certified Nurse Assistant Program (CNAP) is a 5-year, multipronged initiative focused on increasing the CNA workforce across California. CNAP offers resources to employers to create a sustainable employee pipeline and foster CNA retention through career advancement opportunities.

Facilities that are California Department of Public Health (CDPH) approved for facility-based CNA training, or those contracted with Community-based and Online or Alternative CNA training programs, may qualify for Earn and Learn funds.

inventory.text: CNA Employers Long-Term Care Employers Build Your CNA Workforce with CNAP Offering valuable resources and financial awards to long-term care facilities in California designed specifically to recruit, train, and retain a strong and resilient workforce. Employers: Sign Up Now Certified Nurse Assistant Program Certified Nurse Assistant Program (CNAP): Focused on increasing the CNA workforce in California The Certified Nurse Assistant Program (CNAP) is a 5-year, multipronged initiative focused on increasing the CNA workforce across California. CNAP offers resources to employers to create a sustainable employee pipeline and foster CNA retention through career advancement opportunities. Facilities that are California Department of Public Health (CDPH) approved for facility-based CNA training, or those contracted with Community-based and Online or Alternative CNA training programs, may qualify for Earn and Learn funds. Access financial awards and other benefits Learn More Access valuable employer tools, toolkits, and other resources Learn More With CNAP, long-term care facilities across California can build a thriving CNA workforce. CNAP Financial Awards CNAP Benefits Advantages of CNAP Funding Opportunities Gain access to funding options and resources available through CNAP to support your workforce development initiatives. Recruit, Train, Retain (RTR) Leverage CNAP's expertise and resources to enhance your ability to recruit, train, and retain qualified CNAs, ensuring a stable and skilled work environment. Employer Recognition Position your organization as an employer that prioritizes and invests in the development and growth of your frontline workers, fostering a positive workplace culture. Attract Quality Candidates CNAPs reputation as a trusted program attracts quality candidates who actively seek employers that are committed to delivering exceptional care to residents. Enhanced Quality Care Through CNAP's resources and support, you can enhance the quality of care provided to residents by cultivating a skilled and knowledgeable CNA workforce. Continuous Improvement Engage in a culture of continuous improvement as CNAP provides tools, best practices, and educational materials to help your organizations performance. Networking Opportunities Connect and collaborate with other employers, Workforce Investment Boards, or community organizations in the CNAP network, allowing for knowledge sharing, wraparound services and exchange of best practices within and for the CNA industry. CNAP is a Statewide initiative funded by the California Department of Healthcare Access and Information, managed by the Quality Care Health Foundation (QCHF). The goal is to help skilled nursing facilities build a stronger, more stable CNA Workforce and reward you financially for doing it. In 2025 alone, 42 facilities received more than $1 million in awards, and by the first half of 2026, that number climbed to 70 facilities receiving more than $2 million . There’s no cap on what your facility can earn, as long as funds last. Learn How the Program Works Testimonials Oak River Rehab “While the application process at first seemed a bit daunting, once the CNAP team walked me through everything, it was super easy to submit all of the required documents. From there on out, we only saw great benefits through our relationship with CNAP, including the care that our Earn and Learn CNA graduates are now delivering in our facility.” Chad Kanow , Assistant Administrator , Oak River Rehab Kern Valley “CNAP awards have allowed us to continue to offer this program with a reduced demand on facilities resources! It is very easy to work with the CNAP staff! The application process is simple, they explain everything, and it is well organized. We feel incredibly supported!” Brandy Arana, Administrator and NATP Coordinator, Kern Valley Crystal Ridge Care Center "Without knowing the process, the CNAP application can seem a bit daunting, but once you work with the CNAP team, the process is really streamlined, not complicated at all. The staff is so supportive." - Daenen Miller, Administrator, Crystal Ridge Care Center The Pines at Placerville "We just received our first check for the CNAP program for the 18 CNAs that we put through our CNA class. All our interactions with Mai and Zane have been nothing short of amazing. They were with us the entire way and felt invested in our success. Their instructions were clear and concise, and they went above and beyond to ensure we received our reward. We will gladly continue to work with them in future cohorts and are grateful for this partnership." - Colby Hollingsworth, Administrator Southern Inyo Healthcare District “We are thrilled with the CNAP funds received as they have provided us with the financial flexibility to enhance our classrooms and work stations for both our employee students and long-term staff. Thanks to CNAP we can invest in improvements that directly benefit our learning environment and support our educational goals. The process of accessing the funds was straightforward and we appreciate the opportunity to utilize them for our specific needs. CNAP has truly made a positive impact on our facility, and we look forward to our continued partnership.” -Jennifer Emley, Quality Assistant Fallbrook Skilled Nursing “Our experience with the CNAP program has been incredibly beneficial to our facility. With our second cohort of Earn and Learn students graduating soon and another one planned for the near future, CNAP has played a vital role in addressing our staffing needs. Thanks to the Earn and Learn classes, we have significantly reduced our reliance on the CNA registry, saving us $50,000 per month. CNAP’s support has empowered us to build a sustainable workforce and further enhance our patient care and satisfaction. We look forward to our continued partnership.” -Robert Durban, Administrator Golden Heights Healthcare “Thanks to the valuable guidance and support from CNAP staff and the CNAP Resources, our facility navigated the accreditation process and successfully obtained our facility based NATP approval. This achievement not only brought us multiple financial rewards but has also empowered us to hire and train our own CNAs. We are now eagerly preparing to launch an Earn and Learn program, with the goal of building a sustainable and renewable workforce.” -Almaroof Apatira, Administrator Kern Valley Healthcare District "CNAP has aided us with graduating 12 Nurse Assistant Students, successfully passing their state exams to obtain their certifications. The application process is simple and well organized. CNAP awards have allowed us to continue to offer this program with a reduced demand on facilities resources and has offered us a great deal more support than just financial awards. Earn and Learn helps increase our retention of newly trained and certified CNA’s!" -Brandy Arana, LMS Administrator and NATP Coordinator Compass Health, Inc. "Quality Care Health Foundation’s Certified Nursing Assistant Program has been a welcome resource in supporting our goals of training and retaining CNAs. The CNAP program team was easy to work with and supportive throughout the award application and disbursement process. They kept their requests concise, were realistic with deliverable due dates and sent reminders when needed." - Patrick Woolpert, Finance Director Cambridge Health Services "Our experience working with CNAP has been wonderful. Megan was clear and concise with all instructions and also easy to reach if I had any questions. I have felt supported throughout the entire process. As we endeavor to train the best CNAs to support our residents, this grant has made the process so much easier. The support has allowed us to continue to grow our program which only benefits our facilities and residents! We look forward to our future partnership with CNAP in the coming years!" - Jenny Rivera, Cambridge Health Services CNA Upskilling Program (CUSP) The goal of CUSP is to increase and retain the CNA workforce in the long-term care sector by instituting professional recognition of standardized advanced education and training levels, with statewide job titles and incremental financial awards for mastery of duties and wisdom gained. With CUSP, CNAs have the chance to advance through recognized levels of achievement based on their completed educational modules and work experience. As they progress, they’ll not only gain new certifications and skills, but also enjoy the financial rewards that come with each level of accomplishment. Explore CNAP CUSP Certifications Facilities that support CNA upskilling through CUSP may be eligible to receive a financial award.
